profile.bio: CSE undergrad at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda. Software Development Intern at CollegeQuest, building AI-powered career platforms with React Native, FastAPI, and LLMs.
profile.tagline: Full-stack + AI engineer — React Native, FastAPI, LLMs

work_experience.title: Software Development Intern
work_experience.description: Architected and shipped a cross-platform AI education platform using React Native, Expo, TypeScript, Supabase, and FastAPI, delivering 20+ production modules for career planning, college discovery, and AI-powered counselling to students across India. Engineered QuestAI, a streaming AI counsellor with SSE-based authenticated responses, tool-status event handling, animated streaming output, and contextual navigation chips for real-time personalized career guidance. Implemented a full monetization pipeline with token-based billing, plan-aware feature gating, Razorpay checkout integration, and an in-app paywall supporting cross-platform web and native payment redirects. Built AI-powered Career Finder with dynamic quiz generation, personality and skills analysis, career match scoring, and downloadable PDF career reports; developed college discovery engine with AI-assisted comparison and shortlisting across 50,000+ institutions.

work_experience.title: Full Stack Development Intern
work_experience.description: Developed and optimized REST APIs using Node.js, Express.js, PostgreSQL, and Sequelize ORM, supporting scalable job portal workflows and database operations. Built responsive and reusable UI components using Next.js, improving frontend performance and user experience across core modules. Contributed in Agile sprints cycles, delivering feature enhancements, bug fixes, testing, and deployment workflows in a collaborative development environment.

projects.name: parseSkill()
projects.description: An evidence-based developer intelligence platform that analyzes coding profiles and repositories to infer verified technical skills and automatically generate dynamic developer portfolios. Developed a knowledge-graph analytics engine to model relationships between users, projects, technologies, and skills, enabling project intelligence, explainable scoring, and skill evolution tracking. Integrated an XGBoost role prediction model, graph-based recommendation engine, and LLM + RAG assistant to deliver personalized career insights, missing skill analysis and resume optimization.

projects.name: Artive
projects.description: A collaborative creative platform where users share unfinished ideas as "seeds" and others extend them into branching "forks", forming explorable creative lineage trees with unlimited fork depth. Built a semantic search pipeline using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings and MongoDB Atlas vector search to surface contextually relevant seeds, forks, and similar content across the platform. Engineered a cached lineages collection with BFS-based tree traversal for O(n) ancestry resolution, eliminating repeated tree-building computation and enabling low-latency hierarchical rendering in the UI.

projects.title: Fully keyboard-navigable data table
projects.description: Build a sortable/filterable data table that's 100% operable via keyboard and passes an axe-core accessibility audit.
projects.why_this_project: Accessibility is rarely demonstrated in portfolios despite being a frequent interview/requirement topic.

projects.title: Query performance playground
projects.description: Load a large public dataset, write slow queries, then use EXPLAIN ANALYZE and indexes to speed them up 10x+; document each fix.
projects.why_this_project: Query optimization is a rare, high-signal skill most portfolios never demonstrate.

projects.title: Local Kubernetes cluster with autoscaling demo
projects.description: Deploy a small app to kind/minikube with HPA, readiness/liveness probes, and a load test that triggers scale-out.
projects.why_this_project: Watching HPA actually scale under load is far more convincing than a static manifest.

projects.title: End-to-end tabular ML pipeline with drift monitoring
projects.description: Train a model, serve it via FastAPI, and add a feature-drift monitor that alerts when input distribution shifts.
projects.why_this_project: MLOps concerns (drift, monitoring) are what's missing from 90% of 'trained a model' portfolio projects.

projects.title: From-scratch gradient boosting on a Kaggle dataset
projects.description: Implement a simplified gradient boosting classifier from scratch, benchmark against XGBoost on the same dataset.
projects.why_this_project: Implementing the algorithm (not just calling .fit()) proves conceptual understanding.

projects.title: Idempotent ETL pipeline with schema evolution
projects.description: Build a pipeline that ingests changing-schema CSVs into a warehouse table, handling new/removed columns without breaking.
projects.why_this_project: Schema evolution and idempotency are the two things that separate toy ETL scripts from production pipelines.

projects.title: Concurrent job scheduler
projects.description: Build a job scheduler in Go using goroutines/channels with worker pools, backpressure, and graceful shutdown.
projects.why_this_project: Go's concurrency primitives are its whole value proposition — this project can't be faked with a tutorial CRUD app.

projects.title: Zero-copy CSV parser
projects.description: Write a CSV parser in Rust that avoids allocations on the hot path, benchmarked against a naive implementation.
projects.why_this_project: Ownership/borrowing discipline under a performance constraint is exactly what Rust roles screen for.

projects.title: Background job queue with progress streaming
projects.description: Django/FastAPI app that enqueues long-running jobs and streams progress to the browser via SSE/websockets.
projects.why_this_project: Real-time progress feedback is a common product requirement rarely covered in framework tutorials.

projects.title: GraphQL API with DataLoader batching
projects.description: Build a GraphQL API and fix the N+1 query problem using DataLoader; benchmark before/after.
projects.why_this_project: N+1 is the single most common GraphQL production bug — fixing it demonstrates real understanding.
